docs.title: The flash map
docs.text:
Every board has two application slots, ota_0 and ota_1, and an otadata partition that says which of them boots. The bootloader is below the partition table, which is at 0x8000: from 0x0 on the S3 and the C6, and from 0x2000 on the P4.

partitions.csv: 16 MB of flash (the S3, the P4, and a C6 built with sdkconfig.flash16mb)

name      type  offset    size                 what
nvs       data  0x009000  0x006000    24 KiB   the board's name, network and pairings
phy_init  data  0x00F000  0x001000     4 KiB
otadata   data  0x010000  0x002000     8 KiB   which application slot boots
ota_0     app   0x020000  0x400000     4 MiB   application slot; a USB flash writes this one
ota_1     app   0x420000  0x400000     4 MiB   application slot
coredump  data  0x820000  0x010000    64 KiB   a panic's core dump (the S3 image writes none)
audio     data  0x830000  0x040000   256 KiB   the sample stream the partition source reads
storage   fat   0x870000  0x040000   256 KiB   the FAT volume of the fatfs source
reserve   data  0x8B0000  0x400000     4 MiB   unused; the table ends at 0xCB0000

partitions_c6.csv: 4 MB of flash (any C6 module)

nvs       data  0x009000  0x006000    24 KiB
phy_init  data  0x00F000  0x001000     4 KiB
otadata   data  0x010000  0x002000     8 KiB
ota_0     app   0x020000  0x1E0000  1.875 MiB
ota_1     app   0x200000  0x1E0000  1.875 MiB
coredump  data  0x3E0000  0x010000    64 KiB   the table ends at 0x3F0000; no audio, no storage

The two files are partitions.csv and partitions_c6.csv; the OTA plan has the reason for each line.

  • An update over the network writes the slot that is not running, and the new image boots on trial. A reset before the image accepts itself boots the other slot again (CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE). Sink firmware has the sequence.
  • A USB flash writes the bootloader, the partition table, an empty otadata, the application into ota_0, and audio and storage. An empty otadata boots ota_0 with nothing on trial.
  • Nothing writes nvs, which is at 0x9000 in both tables, so a board keeps its name, its network and its pairings through a USB flash and through an update.
  • The partition table, the flash size setting and the bootloader change only over USB. The flash mode (DIO or QIO) is the bootloader's, so it changes only over USB too.

docs.title: Heap floors, and how a refusal is reported
docs.text:
A decoder that cannot allocate calls abort(), which restarts the board and ends its Sendspin session. The floors refuse a play before that point. Each is the least a play can need, and a wider stream asks for more.

  • The boot budget line. After the network is up and the Sendspin player has started, the board prints budget: when=boot net=1 internal_free=... largest=... ask_ring=... ask_decode_stack=... ask_fetch_stack=... ask_total=... ask_biggest=... headroom=... floor=... verdict=.... The asks are the ring and the stacks an HTTP play takes from internal RAM in this build, and headroom is the largest free block less the biggest ask. verdict is ok, short-block (no free block holds the biggest ask), short-total (not that much free in all) or below-floor (the HTTP play floor would refuse).
  • The HTTP play floor, CONFIG_ICLFORGE_EXAMPLE_PLAY_MIN_FREE_BYTES: 160,796 in both C6 profiles and 0 in the others. A POST /play that finds less internal RAM free fails at once: GET /status has "failed": true, "why": "memory" and the bytes that were free in error, and the console has player: a play here needs 160796 bytes of internal RAM free and N are: refused (CONFIG_ICLFORGE_EXAMPLE_PLAY_MIN_FREE_BYTES). A Sendspin stream is not tested by it.
  • The AC-4 floor: 286,365 bytes of heap, PSRAM counted, which is the least any AC-4 stream has needed (the 2.0 probe fixtures' peak). Under it an HTTP play fails with "why": "memory" and player: AC-4 needs at least 286365 bytes of heap and N are free: refused. A Sendspin stream's chunks are refused with the same line under the name burst player:. It came with #1233, and in practice a part with no PSRAM is the one under it.
  • Coded channels over Sendspin, CONFIG_ICLFORGE_EXAMPLE_SENDSPIN_MAX_CODED_CHANNELS: 2 on the C6. A wider syncframe is refused before a decoder is made for it, the console says burst player: refusing a 6-channel syncframe: more than the 2 this part decodes in this build once a stream, and each refused chunk counts as invalid.
  • A lyric document is taken only while internal RAM has three times its size and 8,192 bytes free (twelve times its size when PSRAM has no room for it). Otherwise the console says sendspin: lyrics not taken: N bytes of internal heap free, M needed and the stream plays without lyrics.
  • An allocation that fails anyway prints heap: <function> could not allocate N bytes (caps 0x...); internal free X, largest Y before the abort. tools/checks/check_esp_console.py fails a console capture that has one.

Under QEMU, CI holds the S3's stream set and its Sendspin shape to 20,480 bytes of internal RAM free at the least, and the decode lane's shape to 12,288 (ESP32-S3).

docs.title: ESP32-S3 (N16R8)
docs.text:
The ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1-N16R8: 16 MB of flash and 8 MB of octal PSRAM. Internal RAM is what this board is short of. Wi-Fi, lwIP, two HTTP servers, mDNS, the Sendspin session and the decoder share it, and with Wi-Fi up no free block is over 31,744 bytes.

Figure Build and date Flash 16 MB in QIO mode (sdkconfig.s3-fast). partitions.csv, 4 MiB slots. Budgets: application 1,750,000 bytes (raised from 1,600,000 on 2026-10-25), bootloader 32,768 profiles.json. QIO is worth 8 to 15% of an AC-4 frame and 11 to 19% of an AC-3 or E-AC-3 one: hearth-eb2c64, 2026-10-10 (Playback speed) Internal RAM 524,288 bytes. 32,768 at 0x40370000 are on the instruction bus only: the instruction cache at its 16 KB minimum, and 16 KB of IRAM. 491,520 are addressable as data, and the data cache comes off the top of them Memory Caches Instruction cache 32 KB (sdkconfig.psram), 16 KB over ESP-IDF's minimum and 16 KB of internal RAM. Data cache 64 KB in 64-byte lines (sdkconfig.s3-fast, sdkconfig.s3-dcache), which is 32 KB of the heap (the release image had 32 KB until 2026-10-29) With the 64 KB cache an AC-4 play started with 62 KB free in place of 95: hearth-eb2c64, 2026-10-11 (Playback speed) Code and constants Run from PSRAM (CONFIG_SPIRAM_FETCH_INSTRUCTIONS, CONFIG_SPIRAM_RODATA): 2.3 MB of the 8 MB. The fragment's three settings cost about 1 KB of internal RAM between them sdkconfig.s3-fast, in the release image since 2026-10-11 Static internal RAM 176,854 bytes for s3-n16r8, budget 185,000. No source splits this image into .data and .bss. The default shape with no network is 88,563 bytes, 46,232 of it .bss idf.py size, 2026-10-12 (the profiles plan). The default shape: the README's cost table, which gives no date Heap with no network 304,680 bytes free, largest block 241,664, in the footprint probe, which has a 16 KB instruction cache and a 32 KB data cache. IRAM is 16,384 of 16,384 used, so none of it is donated to the heap QEMU leg, 2026-09-29; a board read 316,196 free on 2026-09-11 (Memory, Contiguity) Heap at boot, Wi-Fi and the Sendspin player up s3-n16r8: 75,503 bytes free at the worst of eight boots (2026-10-29, with the decoder and the 64 KB cache; before it 85,667 to 102,503, and the old s3-n16r8-ac4 66,159 to 82,771) Baseline s3-n16r8 Largest free block, Wi-Fi up 31,744 bytes on all sixteen boots of the two baselines. A 32,768-byte stack in internal RAM cannot be made: such an image answered every POST /play with could not allocate 32768 bytes Baselines; the failure on both boards, main 3d6b2aa0a, 2026-10-12 (sdkconfig.psram) What is in PSRAM The code and constants. Both rings: 32,768 bytes for an HTTP play, 262,144 for Sendspin with its buffers. The decode task's stack for an HTTP play and for a Sendspin stream: 32,768 bytes, 40,960 with AC-4. The decode lane's stack (16,384) and its enhanced-coupling scratch (23 KB), and with AC-4 the second core's worker stack (32,768). Allocations of 16 KB and over. Wi-Fi's and lwIP's buffers, which try PSRAM first. The console's last 16 KiB. A lyric document of up to 2,048 bytes of text profiles.json; The decode stack goes in PSRAM: the stack in PSRAM costs 4 to 5% of a 2.0 A-SPX frame and returns 28 KB of internal RAM, hearth-eb2c64, 2026-10-10 (#1233) The 512-byte rule For the length of an AC-4 play the limit under which malloc tries internal RAM first is CONFIG_ICLFORGE_AC4_INTERNAL_BELOW, 512 bytes on this part. The player puts 16,384 back when the play ends. The decoder then keeps 3 to 14 KB in internal RAM and 0.42 to 1.83 MB in PSRAM. A limit of 4,096 bought 1 to 2% of a frame for 23 to 42 KB of internal RAM, and 8,192 or more left the part 0.4 to 5 KB The split: the AC-4 probe under QEMU, with the decoder as it was before its peaks were cut (Where its memory goes). The sweep: hearth-eb2c64, 2026-10-10 (The 512-byte limit stays) What stays internal The I2S queue, allocated by its capabilities: 12 descriptors of 256 frames, 24 KB at 2.0 in 32-bit slots. Allocations under the limit. Interrupt handlers and the code that runs with the flash cache off What stays in internal RAM, and why Core dump None (CONFIG_ESP_COREDUMP_ENABLE_TO_NONE): it would take 4,016 bytes of internal RAM idf.py size, 2026-09-25 (sdkconfig.psram) Floors No HTTP play floor. The AC-4 floor of 286,365 bytes is met by PSRAM. Boot budget: the one internal ask is the fetch task's 8,192-byte stack, so headroom is 23,552 and verdict is ok Baselines AC-3 5.1 Decoder peak 56,597 bytes. Over Sendspin the least internal heap free was 21 to 79 KB Peak: the probe in float, on a P4 board, 2026-09-23 (What the part carries). Sendspin: S3b on main ce0e099db, 2026-10-12, and the build before it (AC-3 and E-AC-3 in the Hearth player) E-AC-3 5.1 Decoder peak 102,342 bytes with AHT, spectral extension and coupling; 129,657 with enhanced coupling. Over Sendspin the least free was 0.8 to 14 KB As the row above E-AC-3 7.1.4 Decoder peak 167,386 bytes as coded, 173,794 folded to stereo, 195,025 with objects placed onto 7.1.4. Over Sendspin the least free was 23 to 1,100 bytes Peak: QEMU leg, 2026-09-29, equal to the P4 board's. Sendspin: as above AC-4 2.0 Decoder peak 286,365 to 418,110 bytes. An HTTP play took 0.40 to 0.43 MB of PSRAM and left 77 to 80 KB of internal RAM at the least; with the 64 KB cache the plays of every layout left 31 to 49 KB. A Sendspin stream on the old s3-n16r8-ac4 left 83 to 89 KB (on s3-n16r8 since the fold, 47 to 74 KB at the least, 2026-10-29) Peak: the probe (Where its memory goes). Plays: hearth-eb2c64, 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-11 (On the board). Sendspin: S3b, 2026-10-12 (AC-4 from a server) AC-4 5.1 Decoder peak 696,375 to 859,616 bytes. An HTTP play to 5.1 took 0.78 to 1.06 MB of PSRAM and left 72 to 78 KB; the decode stack reached 32,560 bytes in A-CPL mode 3. Over Sendspin the image states 2 channels and a server sends PCM As the row above AC-4 5.1.4 Decoder peak 1,494,319 bytes. An HTTP play to 5.1.4 took 1.71 to 1.82 MB of PSRAM and left 62 to 75 KB. It fits and takes more than twice real time As the row above; the time is on Playback speed

The "least free" figures are low because of where allocations go: those under 16 KB try internal RAM first, so the AC-3 and E-AC-3 decoders and the network fill what is free and then spill to PSRAM. Sending allocations over 4 KB to PSRAM left 80 KB free, a burst then took 28 ms where it had taken 20, and the board underran (In the Sendspin sink, 2026-09-16). What is added to the player's internal allocations is the risk, and the sink guide says how the console reports it.

docs.title: ESP32-C6 (4 MB and 16 MB)
docs.text:
One core, no FPU and no PSRAM: the code runs from flash, and the player's buffers, Wi-Fi's receive buffers and the decoder come out of the same 512 KB. The two images differ in the partition table alone. On this board the limit is memory, and the sink plays AC-3 and E-AC-3 of up to two coded channels (An ESP32-C6 sink).

Figure Build and date Flash QIO mode (sdkconfig.c6). c6-4mb: partitions_c6.csv, 1.875 MiB slots, application budget 1,966,080 bytes, which is the slot. c6-16mb: partitions.csv through sdkconfig.flash16mb, 4 MiB slots, application budget 2,000,000 (raised from 1,880,000 on 2026-10-25). Bootloader budget 32,768 profiles.json. The image was 1,665,856 bytes on 2026-09-25, 91% of a 1.75 MiB slot (the OTA plan). QIO left about 8% of the part idle where DIO left 1%: AC-3 2.0 over Wi-Fi, 2026-09-17 (sdkconfig.c6) Cache 16 KB for code and data together, in 32-byte lines. The fixed-point transform's tables are initialised data (.data) for that reason: as constants in flash they cost 15 thousandths of a burst (AC-3 656 to 671, E-AC-3 751 to 766) The cache: ESP-IDF's ROM header for the part. The timing: the C6 board, c6-16mb (#1511, merged 2026-10-13) Wi-Fi's code In flash: CONFIG_ESP_WIFI_IRAM_OPT, _EXTRA_IRAM_OPT, _RX_IRAM_OPT, _SLP_IRAM_OPT and CONFIG_ESP_PHY_IRAM_OPT are off (sdkconfig.sendspin-c6). In the probe's Wi-Fi build that took the code in RAM from 93,190 to 44,804 bytes and the heap free at boot from 295,104 to 343,968, and AC-3 5.1 from 0.82 to 1.09 of real time The probe, 2026-09-15 (WiFi's code kept in flash) Static internal RAM 111,823 bytes for both images, budget 117,000: .bss 43,664, .data 21,655, and the rest code placed in RAM. It was 144,139 (.bss 81,736) before 27,776 bytes of the decoder's tables came out, and 116,307 (.bss 53,904) after idf.py size, 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13 (#1474, #1511, the profiles plan) Heap with no network 383,416 bytes free, largest block 352,256, in the footprint probe The probe on a board, 2026-09-15 (Memory) Heap at boot, Wi-Fi and the Sendspin player up 136,668 to 140,304 bytes free, largest block 118,784 to 124,928 Baseline c6-16mb. Before #1474 the worst boot of eight was 108,792 free and 88,064 largest (v0.10.0-beta.1-4520-g26274cd77, 2026-10-12) What a Sendspin stream takes A 49,152-byte ring, a 24,576-byte decode stack, chunks of at most 4,096 bytes, no delay lines and no lyric document (sdkconfig.sendspin-c6). A 64 KB ring left a largest block of 1,824 bytes, and two 1,848-byte Wi-Fi receive buffers could not be allocated 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-20 (sdkconfig.sendspin-c6) What an HTTP play takes 134,008 bytes: the ring (32,768), the decode stack (32,768), the fetch stack (8,192), the I2S queue (12,672) and the smallest decoder (47,608, AC-3 1/0) sdkconfig.sendspin-c6 I2S queue 12 descriptors of 256 frames in 16-bit slots: 12,288 bytes and 384 of descriptors at 2.0, and 49 KB for eight TDM slots sdkconfig.sendspin-c6 Core dump and log A core dump is kept, for 1,140 bytes of static RAM. GET /log keeps the console's last 2 KiB idf.py size, 2026-09-25 (sdkconfig.defaults) Opus While an Opus stream plays, 27,060 bytes of decoder state and about 16.4 KB of the 24 KB decode stack The Hearth sink's image with Wi-Fi up (Opus from a server, on that page since 2026-10-11) Floors An HTTP play needs 160,796 bytes of internal RAM free: the 134,008 above and the 26,788 that a Sendspin E-AC-3 stream left the network at the least. The board has 136,668 to 140,304 at boot, so every HTTP play is refused and the boot budget line says verdict=below-floor. A Sendspin stream of more than 2 coded channels is refused. An image built with the AC-4 decoder refuses an AC-4 play under 286,365 bytes Baseline c6-16mb: both HTTP rows end failed, why memory. The floor was 134,008 until #1474 freed enough RAM for a play to start and fail AC-3 2.0 Decoder peak 49,328 bytes. Over Sendspin the least internal heap free was 56,104 Peak: the probe, fixed point, 2026-09-15. Sendspin: baseline c6-16mb E-AC-3 2.0 Decoder peak 108,094 bytes on 2026-09-15; a 2.0 stream with coupling has held 24,576 bytes less since #1494. Over Sendspin the least free was 25,836 Peak: the probe, fixed point. Sendspin: baseline c6-16mb AC-3 5.1 and E-AC-3 5.1 Decoder peaks 56,685 and 164,066 bytes (109,806 for E-AC-3 since). Both fit the probe with Wi-Fi up. In the sink each stopped within about 12 seconds on a failed allocation, and both are refused now Peaks: 2026-09-15 (Memory). The sink: 2026-09-22; not run again since the decoder got smaller (An ESP32-C6 sink) E-AC-3 7.1.4 Decoder peak 227,662 bytes (174,850 on the CI probe since). It did not fit the probe's Wi-Fi build with ESP-IDF's IRAM options on, and is refused in the sink 2026-09-15 (ESP32-C6) AC-4 Decoder peak in fixed point: 286,365 to 426,918 bytes at 2.0, 704,311 to 868,424 at 5.1, 1,502,903 at 5.1.4. With the sink up a play started with 117,328 bytes free and is refused. A C6 is sent AC-4 as PCM Peaks: the Cortex-M3 leg, 2026-10-03. The board: hearth-db4c40, 2026-10-10 (AC-4, #1233)

Static RAM is what this board's heap is the remainder of. The 27,776 bytes that #1474 took out were function-local tables of coding tools a stereo stream never uses: enhanced coupling's (10,240 and 5,536), transient pre-noise's (3,072) and the double MDCT tables that only the object decoder's direct-form branches named (8,928). Before it, an E-AC-3 stream over Sendspin left 0.9 to 4.5 KB and failed after an AC-3 stream in the same boot.

docs.title: ESP32-P4 (v1.x, and v3.x with the panel)
docs.text:
The P4 has the most internal RAM and 32 MB of PSRAM, and no radio: Wi-Fi is the board's ESP32-C6, over SDIO. Its two chip generations take two images that refuse each other's chips (An ESP32-P4 sink). Everything measured here is from a DFRobot FireBeetle 2, chip revision v1.3.

Figure Build and date Chip revision p4-rev1: revisions v1.0 to v1.99, 360 MHz. p4-rev3: v3.1 to v3.99, 400 MHz, the lyric panel profiles.json; p4-rev3 has not run on a board (The chip revision) Flash 16 MB in QIO mode at 80 MHz (sdkconfig.p4). partitions.csv, 4 MiB slots. p4-rev3's application budget is 2,900,000 bytes (raised from 2,600,000 on 2026-10-25); 473 KB of that image is fonts QIO took 14 to 25% off an AC-4 frame and 4 to 8% off AC-3 and E-AC-3: 2026-10-02 (Flash mode). The p4-rev3 build was 2,469,920 bytes on 2026-10-12 Bootloader In the 24,576 bytes from 0x2000 to the partition table. v1.x at the Info log level with QIO: 24,368 bytes, 208 to spare. v3.x is 25,152 at Info, so p4-rev3 builds it at the Warn level: 22,448 sdkconfig.p4; sdkconfig.p4-rev3, a build of 2026-10-12 Internal RAM 768 KB. The footprint probe, with no network and no PSRAM, had 514,820 bytes free at boot and a largest block of 385,024 The probe on a board, 2026-09-23 (Memory) The low-power SRAM 32 KB at 0x50108000, reached with no cache: 174 to 195 cycles an access against 6 to 7 for main RAM. CONFIG_ESP_SYSTEM_ALLOW_RTC_FAST_MEM_AS_HEAP=n keeps it out of the heap, which is 32,640 bytes smaller. With it in, the 29.97 fps converter took 93.8 ms a frame; with it out, 12.0 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-02 (The low-power SRAM, #1176). The 8 KB of tightly coupled memory at 0x30100000 is still in the heap and was not measured Caches A 16 KB instruction cache and a 128 KB L2 cache in 64-byte lines. The firmware is copied into PSRAM at start and runs from there (CONFIG_SPIRAM_XIP_FROM_PSRAM): 1.4 MB of code and 0.8 MB of constants in the AC-4 image, 14 KB more image and no internal RAM 14 to 36% less time a frame on one core: 2026-10-11 (The firmware in PSRAM and the second core) Static internal RAM 166,948 bytes for p4-rev3, budget 175,000. The v1.x profiles have no budget and no source gives their figure or a .data and .bss split idf.py size on a build of 2026-10-12 (the profiles plan) Heap at boot, Wi-Fi and the Sendspin player up p4-rev1, with the AC-4 decoder since 2026-10-29: 295,671 to 312,299 free, largest 208,896 to 212,992 (without it, as the profile was before: 291,783 to 291,803 free, largest 217,088 to 221,184) The p4-rev1 baseline, which is the old p4-rev1-ac4's What is in PSRAM The firmware. Both rings: 32,768 and 262,144 bytes. Allocations of 16 KB and over. The SDIO link's buffers, about 31 blocks of 1,536 bytes (CONFIG_ESP_HOSTED_MEMPOOL_PREFER_SPIRAM). The decode lane's stack (16,384). The console's last 16 KiB. A lyric document of up to 16,384 bytes of text profiles.json, sdkconfig.p4 What stays internal The decode task's stack: 32,768 bytes, 40,960 with AC-4, of which the decoder uses 19 to 30 KB. The I2S queue: 12 descriptors of 256 frames, 24 KB at 2.0; a sixteen-slot TDM frame would be 196 KB. With AC-4, the second core's worker stack for an HTTP play: 24,576 bytes. A core dump is kept, for 3,652 bytes of static RAM Stack use: 2026-10-02 (What the decoder holds). The worker's stack: firmware/esp-idf/iclforge/src/player.cpp. Core dump: idf.py size, 2026-09-25 Allocation policy ESP-IDF's: under 16,384 bytes internal RAM first, and CONFIG_ICLFORGE_AC4_INTERNAL_BELOW is 16,384 here. A 512-byte limit left 281 to 298 KB of internal RAM free and took 1.08 to 1.24 times as long a frame The twenty plays, 2026-10-02 (Allocation policy) The panel (p4-rev3) All in PSRAM: the frame buffer (1,228,800 bytes: 1024 by 600 at 16 bits), two render buffers of 81,920, LVGL's heap and glyph caches (about 100 KB for each of four faces at its largest), and the screen task's 16,384-byte stack sdkconfig.panel, profiles.json. The drawing's cost was measured on the v1.3 board with no panel (Memory and time) Floors No HTTP play floor. The AC-4 floor of 286,365 bytes is met by PSRAM. Over Sendspin the AC-4 image states 6 channels, so a 5.1.4 stream is refused there and sent as PCM. An E-AC-3 stream that declares more than 12 objects is played as its bed Board 1, 2026-10-12 (AC-4 from a server) AC-3 5.1 Decoder peak 56,597 bytes. An AC-3 2.0 stream over Sendspin left 253,939 bytes of internal heap at the least Peak: the probe, 2026-09-23 (What the part carries). Sendspin: baseline p4-rev1 E-AC-3 5.1 Decoder peak 102,342 bytes. An E-AC-3 2.0 stream over Sendspin left 203,315 bytes; E-AC-3 5.1 on the AC-4 image left 211 to 218 KB Peak: as above. Sendspin: baseline p4-rev1; board 1, 2026-10-12 E-AC-3 7.1.4 Decoder peak 167,386 bytes as coded; the stream set's eleven files peak at 80,922 to 256,584. Over Sendspin the internal RAM left was never under 108 KB Peaks: the probe, 2026-09-23 (Stream set). Sendspin: board 1, main ce0e099db, 2026-10-12 (AC-3 and E-AC-3 in the Hearth player) AC-4 2.0 An HTTP play's peak heap was 0.58 to 0.63 MB, internal RAM and PSRAM together, and it left 4 KB of internal RAM at the least. A Sendspin stream left 14 to 28 KB, and 2.9 KB through the frame-rate converter HTTP: the second FireBeetle 2, 2026-10-02 (Decode time and memory). Sendspin: board 1, 2026-10-12 (AC-4 from a server) AC-4 5.1 An HTTP play to 5.1 peaked at 1.06 to 1.36 MB and left 2 to 8 KB of internal RAM. A Sendspin stream left 3.9 to 31 KB As the row above AC-4 5.1.4 An HTTP play to 5.1.4 peaked at 2.06 to 2.18 MB and left 1 KB of internal RAM. It is refused over Sendspin As the row above

An AC-4 play uses up this board's internal RAM, and the profile leaves it so. Under ESP-IDF's policy the decoder's many blocks of 8 to 16 KB go to internal RAM until it is full, and its large blocks go to PSRAM: 0.24 MB at 2.0, 0.7 to 1.0 MB at 5.1 and 1.7 to 1.8 MB at 5.1.4. That is the faster arrangement here, where PSRAM behind its caches costs the same as main RAM when the data is cached. A board that is also updated over the network or sent a lyric document during an AC-4 stream has not been run (AC-4 from a server).

docs.title: What to keep out of internal RAM
docs.text:
• Any single block near the largest free block. On an S3 with Wi-Fi up that is 31,744 bytes. A 32 KB stack or a ring goes to PSRAM by name (CONFIG_ICLFORGE_EXAMPLE_DECODE_STACK_IN_PSRAM, ..._SENDSPIN_DECODE_STACK_IN_PSRAM, ..._RING_IN_PSRAM) and is asked for with PSRAM capabilities. malloc's size rule does not apply to a task's stack, which FreeRTOS takes from internal RAM unless the task is created with capabilities.
  • Function-local static tables of optional coding tools. They are .bss in every image, whether or not a stream uses the tool: 27,776 bytes on the C6 (#1474). Make the table a member of the heap object that exists only while the tool runs, or a constant in flash.
  • Constants, where a cache miss is cheap. On the S3 and the P4 the code and constants run from PSRAM. On the C6 a table the decoder reads in every block stays in .data, because the 16 KB cache is shared with the code (#1511).
  • thread_local buffers. FreeRTOS takes each task's thread-local area from that task's stack and sizes it from the whole image. A 32 KB thread_local scratch made every task's area 32 KB, ESP-IDF's IPC task has a 1 KB stack, and the S3 application failed before app_main (What the port required from the library).
  • Documents made of many small blocks. A parsed lyric document is about ten times its text at the peak, and every block is under the 16 KB limit. The Sendspin player reads and holds it with PSRAM first for that one task (PsramScope).
  • Buffers that keep their largest size. Three Sendspin receive buffers kept the capacity of the largest message they had held: an 8,000-byte lyric document left 12.7 KB of an S3's internal heap taken for the rest of the connection. A JSON document over 4,096 bytes now releases them, and audio chunks keep theirs so that a stream does not allocate for every chunk (#1408: S3a, 2026-10-12).
  • The P4's low-power SRAM. A project of its own that decodes on a P4 sets CONFIG_ESP_SYSTEM_ALLOW_RTC_FAST_MEM_AS_HEAP=n.
  • A second graphics heap. LVGL's allocator is PSRAM alone (CONFIG_LV_USE_CUSTOM_MALLOC), because ESP-IDF's malloc would put every block under 16 KB in internal RAM.

Two things belong in internal RAM. DMA buffers are allocated by their capabilities and no limit moves them. And moving the decoder's working memory to PSRAM costs time: 1.08 to 1.24 times a frame on the P4, and enough on the S3's E-AC-3 decode to underrun. The S3's 512-byte rule holds for AC-4 plays alone, where the alternative left Wi-Fi with 0.4 to 5 KB.

docs.title: How to measure
docs.text:
Static RAM, from a build:

  • idf.py size --format json2 gives DIRAM, and python tools/hearth/sink_profile.py verify <profile> --build-dir <dir> --size-json <file> holds it, the application and the bootloader to the profile's budgets. CI runs both for every profile it builds.
  • idf.py size-components and idf.py size-files give the same by archive and by object file.
  • For .bss by input section, read the linker map in the build directory. An archive's own total can differ from the linked image's: the three copies of one table in libiclforge_ac3_minimal.a are one weak symbol after the link, 39,864 bytes in the archive and 39,752 in the image. tools/checks/footprint_report.py reads a GNU ld map the same way for the Cortex-M3 probe.
  • idf.py size's "remain" is the linker's estimate of the heap. On the S3 probe it said 239,164 where the allocator reported 304,680.

The heap, from a running board. The firmware has no heap route; it prints these lines, and GET /log returns the console's recent output (the last 16 KiB on a board with PSRAM, 2 KiB on the C6; python tools/hearth/ota.py log --host <board> --follow follows it):

  • budget: at boot and when a network comes up later: free, the largest block, the asks and the verdict (above).
  • sendspin: player up with internal heap N free, largest block M when the Sendspin player starts.
  • heap: internal free N (largest block M), psram free P when an HTTP play has opened its source, before the decoder allocates.
  • sendspin.progress ... heap_free=N heap_largest=M heap_least=L every 125 chunks of a Sendspin stream, and sendspin.stream= ... heap_free=L when it ends: the least internal heap free while the stream played.
  • stream.decode_stack_free=N at the end of an HTTP play, and decode_stack_free and server_stack_free in GET /status's sendspin object.
  • ac4.heap internal_start=... internal_least=... internal_peak=... psram_start=... psram_least=... psram_peak=... at the end of an AC-4 play.
  • GET /hardware has psram_bytes, profile and profile_hash, and GET /firmware has the partition table and both slots.

To hold a board to figures:

  • tools/checks/check_esp_console.py --min-heap-free <bytes> --min-budget-headroom <bytes> on a console capture. --budget-verdict below-floor is the C6's.
  • python tools/hearth/board_suite.py run --profile <profile> --restart --boots 8 --repeat 5 with --record or --compare <baseline>, on a booked bench board.
  • tools/checks/run_esp32s3_probe.sh, and with --ac4, for the decoder alone under QEMU: peak heap for each fixture and, for AC-4, the internal RAM and PSRAM each took.
  • On an S3 image with AC-4, ?below=N in a play's location sets that play's allocation limit.

docs.title: Traps
docs.text:
• An update over the network overwrites the slot that is not running. One push leaves the image the board had as the one to go back to. A second push overwrites it. After two pushes the image the board was found on is in neither slot, and restoring it means pushing that image again.
  • A P4 board's chip revision decides the image. A v1.x image refuses a v3.x chip and the other way round. GET /hardware and esptool chip-id say which a board is, and ota.py chooses from them (Sink firmware). On v1.x, 400 MHz asserts in a boot loop.
  • The flash mode is the bootloader's. An application built for QIO runs at DIO speed under a DIO bootloader, and an update over the network keeps the bootloader. A board takes QIO with one USB flash that includes its bootloader.
  • The P4's bootloader has 24,576 bytes. A new ESP-IDF, a log level or a chip revision can take it over, and the build then fails.
  • The largest free block decides an allocation. A C6 with 11,016 bytes free could not allocate a 1,848-byte Wi-Fi buffer: no block was over 1,824.
  • QEMU has no Wi-Fi. The S3's release shape under QEMU boots with 226,679 bytes free and a 135,168-byte largest block, where a board has about 86,000 and 31,744. A stack that cannot be made on a board is made there.
  • A low-water mark depends on what played before. On an S3 an AC-3 stream after an E-AC-3 one read 7.2 KB free where the first stream of a boot read 58 to 60 KB. Record a board's figures after a restart, in a fixed order.
  • Freeing RAM can defeat a floor. The C6's HTTP play floor refused every play only while the board had too little free to pass it. With 27,776 bytes back a play started and failed, and the floor went from 134,008 to 160,796.
  • CONFIG_SPIRAM_MALLOC_RESERVE_INTERNAL reserves nothing for long. ESP-IDF v6.1 lets ordinary small allocations take the reserve once the rest of internal RAM is full.
